conbody.p: The outline on the left lists the tasks, numbered as an outline (1, 1.1, 1.2, 2). A task with sub-tasks has an arrow that folds them away. The figure at the end of each row is the task's progress. Select a task's title, or its bar, to show it in the panel beside the chart. The small open button at the end of the row opens the task in full, as the board does: its description, assignee, linked artifacts, to-dos and activity. A milestone's open button shows the milestone beside the chart.
On the timeline, each task is a bar from its start to its due date:

ul.li: The bar fills from the left as the task progresses.
A green bar is a task in Done. A red bar is late: it is past its due date and not done.
A task with sub-tasks is drawn as a thinner, darker bar that spans all of them: see Tasks with sub-tasks.

An arrow joins two related tasks, from the task that drives to the task it drives. Where it leaves and arrives shows the type of the relationship: see Relationships between tasks. A dashed red arrow is a relationship the dates break; the outline marks that task with a warning sign.
With Critical path on, a thin line after a bar, ended by a tick, is the task's float: how far its end can slip before it pushes the next task.
A task with no dates yet has an empty row that you click, or drag across, to schedule it.
Days the plan does not work are shaded at the Days scale: see Working days.

conbody.p: The row of Milestones above the tasks holds a diamond for each milestone, with its name and progress. The thin band leading up to a diamond, from the milestone before it, fills as that milestone's criteria are met. The red vertical line is today.

Days, Weeks, Months and Quarters change the scale. The page opens at the scale that shows the whole plan, on the whole plan. A plan too long to fit opens with today a third of the way in from the left, so that most of what you see is ahead of you.
On a computer the chart reaches the bottom of the window, and so does the panel of a task or a milestone opened beside it; each scrolls on its own when it is longer than the window.

The timeline scrolls sideways past both ends of the plan, further forward than back: use the scroll bar, a trackpad or a wheel, or drag an empty part of the timeline. The scroll bar under the chart belongs to the timeline, so it starts where the task column ends. Today scrolls the timeline so that today sits a third of the way in from the left.
The figures above the chart count the plan: how far it is complete, its tasks, those done, late, on the critical path and not yet scheduled, the effort in it, and the milestones met.
